# Results — Study 290 (September-Effect) on the Shiller S&P 500 monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). S&P 500 monthly
**price** returns are computed from the Shiller monthly dataset
(`_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`, staged in the repo-level cache), 1950–2025.
Price-only — dividends excluded. Match the fingerprint below to confirm you
hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 (nominal price, month-over-month) | 1950–2025 | 912 months (76 Septembers) | `b4e287ff931c` |

## The base rate — the key number

The S&P 500 finished **up in 62.7%** of all 912 months in the window. So any
"this month is down" claim must be measured against a market that rises most of
the time. The honest comparison for September is the **pooled other-month
mean**, not zero.

## Per-calendar-month profile (mean monthly price return)

| Month | Mean %/mo | Std %/mo | Up-rate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Jan | +1.413 | 3.16 | 67.1% | +4.21 |
| Feb | +0.754 | 3.57 | 55.3% | +1.83 |
| Mar | +0.430 | 3.83 | 59.2% | +1.04 |
| Apr | +1.224 | 2.95 | 72.4% | +3.55 |
| May | +0.720 | 3.55 | 60.5% | +2.28 |
| Jun | +0.465 | 3.21 | 60.5% | +1.16 |
| Jul | +0.707 | 3.24 | 64.5% | +1.65 |
| Aug | +0.426 | 3.64 | 60.5% | +1.10 |
| **Sep** | **+0.000** | 3.67 | **57.9%** | **+0.00** |
| Oct | −0.063 | 3.91 | 53.9% | −0.18 |
| Nov | +1.352 | 3.81 | 67.1% | +2.93 |
| Dec | +1.262 | 2.65 | 73.7% | +4.81 |

September is essentially **flat (+0.00%/mo)** — the famous laggard. Honest
twist: in this window **October** is the only month that is actually negative
(−0.06%/mo). "September is the worst month" is a slogan; September is the
*weakest of the up months*, and October is the lone negative one.

## September vs the rest — the core inference

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| September mean | **+0.00%/mo** |
| Other-month mean | **+0.79%/mo** |
| Gap (Sep − rest) | **−0.79pp/mo** |
| September up-rate | 57.9% (vs 62.7% base rate) |
| **Newey-West HAC *t* on the Sep dummy** | **−1.93** |
| Welch two-sample *t* (Sep vs rest) | −1.81 (p = 0.074) |
| One-sided permutation *p* (drag) | 0.034 |

- The **HAC *t* = −1.93** is the headline. It leans clearly negative but **does
  not clear the robust |t| ≥ 2 bar** — so the Signal is **WEAK**, not REAL.
- The **permutation *p* = 0.034** looks significant, but it assumes months are
  i.i.d. The HAC test corrects for the mild serial correlation in monthly
  returns and is the more conservative, more honest number. When the two
  disagree at the margin, the robust test governs.
- The Welch *p* = 0.074 agrees: directionally right, not significant at 5%.

## Sub-period persistence — the drag is not stable

| Period | September mean | HAC *t* | n Septembers |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1950–1985 | **+0.225%/mo** | +0.41 | 36 |
| 1986–2005 | **−0.923%/mo** | −1.09 | 20 |
| 2006–2025 | **+0.518%/mo** | +0.90 | 20 |

The drag lives almost entirely in **1986–2005** (the era of the 1987 crash, the
2001 dot-com autumn, and the September runs into the 2008 crisis). It is mildly
*positive* both before and after. A genuine structural seasonal would persist;
this looks like a handful of bad autumns clustered in one window — strong
evidence against an exploitable effect.

## The n = 76 problem

With only 76 Septembers and ~3.7% September monthly volatility, the minimum
detectable Sep-vs-rest gap at 80% power (two-sided, α = 0.05) is ≈ 0.92pp/mo.
The observed gap is −0.79pp/mo — about 86% of the MDE, i.e. **right on the edge
of detectability**. One month a year simply does not accumulate enough data.

## Could you trade it? — the avoid-September rule

Hold the S&P every month except September (cash, 0% in September). Two trades a
year (exit end-August, re-enter end-September) at 5 bps one-way.

| Strategy | Annualised (price-only) |
|---|--:|
| Buy & hold | **+8.253%/yr** |
| Avoid September (gross) | +8.326%/yr (edge **+0.07pp**) |
| Avoid September (net of 2 trades/yr) | +8.226%/yr (edge **−0.03pp**) |

The gross edge is a **rounding error**; net of trading it is **negative**; and
on a taxable book, selling every August realises gains that compound the drag.
Cash earns 0% here (conservative); in a high-rate regime cash would earn the
risk-free rate and help — but the realised-gains tax and the borderline,
non-persistent signal leave no robust edge.

## Positive control — the machinery finds a drag when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_monthly`), planting a
September drag and sweeping its size recovers it cleanly:

| Planted drag (bps/mo) | Gap (pp/mo) | HAC *t* | Verdict |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| 0 (null) | ~0 | ~0 | below bar (correct) |
| −200 | ~−2.0 | ~−3.4 | clears |t| ≥ 2 |
| −500 | ~−4.4 | ~−10 | clears |
| −1000 | ~−9.4 | ~−22 | clears |

The engine works; the real tape's −0.79pp/mo gap sits at the edge of
detectability with n = 76. The verdict is a statement about the **market and
sample size**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** September genuinely lags by −0.79pp/mo and is well-attested
  in the literature, but the serial-correlation-robust HAC *t* = −1.93 falls
  short of |t| ≥ 2, the Welch test is non-significant (p = 0.074), and the drag
  fails the persistence check (concentrated in 1986–2005). Real-leaning, not
  robustly proven.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Avoiding September gains +0.07pp/yr gross and
  −0.03pp/yr net (before tax). There is no exploitable edge — the soft month is
  real, the trade is not.
- **Honesty notes.** Returns are **price-only** (the total-return September gap
  is even smaller); the S&P *index* is reconstituted, so the measured drag is an
  upper bound on what a fixed-membership basket would show.
